answers.answer: For each held office card, roll one die simultaneously, adding one per fatigue and one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the officeholder. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make normal office attrition rolls.
answers.evidence: “Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.” Retirees go to Pensioners; card flips into Vacant Offices; fatigue returns to supply.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. An acting player may peek at display blackmails. There is no immediate replacement; if the display empties, skip remaining eligible players. After this step, discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: “Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows ... then clockwise from PM.”

answers.answer: Each player chooses one family action and places their opportunity marker on it. If it was already on that action at phase start, that action may be taken twice. A law-granted extra action is separate: only the latest passed extra-action law is usable, it is not doubled by the marker, and it does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action places two writers plus one additional writer once that turn, for three total.
answers.evidence: “If your marker was already on that action at phase start, you may take that action twice”; extra law action gets no marker doubling. With at least four vacant offices, Writer places one additional writer once this turn.

answers.answer: After family actions, while both Company Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court as a Company share and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. If Debt is gone, slide the remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The initial Seek Share payment goes to the bank, not Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: “If Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat”; with no Debt, slide applicants right preserving order. “Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.”

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending order by the number on the backs of their cards. Hiring your own family normally requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer the office’s fatigue to the new card and place the old card, now vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip hiring: the office remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: “Fill vacant offices in ascending number”; own-family hiring requires consent of “every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool”; transfer fatigue to new card; old card reinserted vacant. If no candidate/hirer, skip.

answers.answer: The former Chairman announces a pure majority of current shares, meaning more than half. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody reaches the announced majority, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, using a member from supply or, if needed and possible, from a prize (losing that prize’s VP); if that is impossible, there is no Chairman. The Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
answers.evidence: “Move one winner’s Company shares into Chairman slot ... It still counts as a share ... but cannot be traded or invested in firms.” Deadlock fallback: former Chairman picks any shareholder including self.

answers.answer: For a Company-office check, first commit resources and pay any cash from that acting office’s treasury to the bank; gather dice and subtract penalties, then roll. The lowest die determines the result: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retryable if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure, ending that office’s actions, returning its officeholder to supply, discarding fatigue, and flipping its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading without a ship or deploying without dice just to trigger potential officer losses.
answers.evidence: “all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank”; lowest die 1–2 / 3–4 / 5–6 outcomes; catastrophic destinations and dead-action examples specified.

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, receiving £5 Balance for each, and may take each additional advance only with consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (the Chairman counts). Debt cannot go beyond the track end. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while observing the borrowing limits. Money already in office treasuries stays there for those offices.
answers.evidence: “May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling majority Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance…”

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend from its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship may be placed in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships last only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: “Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains”; prices and placement destinations listed. Company ship purchase requires “no ships remain on shipyards.”

answers.answer: The President declares regions for Trade, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 in the President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried during that President’s uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. A successful Trade can occur at most once per President per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and subsequent orders must be adjacent to an order already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another President’s home region, even if that office is vacant. Company Balance rises by each order’s printed revenue, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 per order and writer owners £1 per placed writer.
answers.evidence: Trade procedure states declared regions, one die per £1, −1 per nonhome region, retries and one successful Trade; route, writers/tokens, protected home regions and bonuses are specified.

answers.answer: A Commander may target its Presidency’s home region, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region, but not another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for Deploy to have an effect. Exhausted officers/regiments each supply one die; local alliances supply their printed dice. Subtract the strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting target once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check; noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die for each officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments never roll officer losses.
answers.evidence: “Target own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region”; resource dice and empire-strength penalty described. “After each attempt” roll for exhausted officers; each 6 removes one.

answers.answer: On successful Deploy, loot equals £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot-token modifier, with a minimum of one plus the number of surviving used officers. Distribute the available loot in repeating cycles: £1 to the Commander, £1 per used surviving officer they had, £1 clockwise for each other player’s used surviving officer, then £1 to the bank per regiment and per alliance piece (regardless of alliance strength), repeating until cash is exhausted. The Commander gains one trophy per target tower. For control, remove the tower/dome; if the target was a capital, remove all matching empire flags; open all orders and clear unrest. If newly Company-controlled, put the loot/control token region-side above the President; place a Governor overlay there and its office card in Vacant Offices. If the Elephant is there pointing outward, put it fully inside for Rebellion. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies, rounded up, and the Commander member returns to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and no office card is vacated.
answers.evidence: Deploy section gives loot formula and distribution cycle, trophies and control changes; catastrophe returns half trophies rounded up and member, with officer loss rolls still made.

answers.answer: A Governor takes its printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one. Success pays the Governor £1, plus £1 more if the previous roll failed, and allows a choice: build a Company ship (one success places it partially built in that region; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone linked to the Governor’s President), commission a regiment into that President’s Army, or Tax by adding £2 unsplit to Balance or the President’s treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in that region. Every unsuccessful check adds unrest. The Governor may continue until choosing to stop, running out of dice, or suffering catastrophe; catastrophe follows normal office removal.
answers.evidence: Administer specifies current dice pool and decrement, success payment/bonus and three choices, Tax unrest after first, unrest on each unsuccessful check, and stopping/catastrophe conditions.

answers.answer: Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 for every existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones (including China); Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one per loan until the track ends, and continue taking loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt creates no extra expense this turn. After loans, set Balance to zero; one or two loans reduce Standing by one, while three or more reduce it by two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations for current Standing; if below, reduce Standing one. Finally, the Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per Company share per dividend, including the Chairman’s share. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.
answers.evidence: Revenue sequence explicitly covers expense items, emergency loans through/at max Debt, no same-turn expense, zero Balance and Standing changes, then expectations and dividends.

answers.answer: A Crisis against a Company region triggers the primary attack first, followed by secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; within each Presidency its Commander orders its attacks. A primary normal Crisis uses normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die (no unrest). Each secondary Rebellion uses only that region’s number of unrest cubes, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. If exhausted strength is insufficient, the region is lost. Otherwise clear all unrest and the Commander gains one trophy. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts instead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gains/loses no trophies, and no Commander is appointed. A successful defense thus exhausts those pieces, clears unrest and awards the Commander a trophy; for a primary Invasion, successful defense also means the attack failed, so remove one tower from the attacker if possible.
answers.evidence: “Resolve primary first; then Bombay, Madras, Bengal”; strength distinctions listed. Defense: exhaust required pieces, insufficient means loss, otherwise clear unrest and trophy; vacant Commander substitution and no trophies.

answers.answer: The PM reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one (a dilemma forces a choice and ends drawing), discards the others, selects the matching policy space, and sets Vote to the law’s printed starting support. Voting begins with the PM and proceeds clockwise through cash votes (£1 per vote) and printed card votes; support may move either way. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. Players who voted for may later oppose, but once opposing cannot support that vote again. The largest opposition total holds Opposition Leader (a tie preserves the current holder); consented votes on behalf of a player who opposes or commits to oppose count for that player. PM may not oppose or consent to enterprise opposition except forced by the named promise. At support −1 or less, the law fails: discard it, resolve any dilemma’s failure text, pass the PM dial to the Opposition Leader, and have the new PM move the proposed policy one space either way and resolve that adjacent policy. At support zero or more, the law passes: keep it with passed laws, give PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then immediate law effects. In either result, restore used voting cards to regular orientation at the end. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament section states thresholds: “−1 or less fails” with failure sequence and “Zero or higher passes” with policy then immediate law effects; voting details and card reset specified.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passage, reduce Debt by one for each two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no accompanying policy; failure does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. 1813 starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: “In 1758/Long 1710 ... may ... if ... lined ... and must if either on starred”; pass/fail effects and exceptions stated; 1813 begins deregulated.

answers.answer: During the Firms phase after family share creation and before Hiring, form a firm by returning one eligible Company share to supply or flipping a workshop to its invested side; the family board flips, a family member becomes its first firm share, its value cube starts at the leftmost space, and £5 from the bank goes to its London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, with its manager’s consent, contribute the same kind of share/workshop, creating one firm share and putting £5 from the bank into London. Firms can have up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman’s share cannot be used. Company shares cannot be used for investment when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and shares created this turn cannot be used even if traded away. Invested workshops never revert to uninvested and give no workshop bonus or Company-failure VP; they stay invested even if the firm fails.
answers.evidence: Firms phase specifies Form and Invest contributions, bank source and London destination of £5; ten-share cap, Chairman/lined-space/new-share restrictions; workshops remain invested.

answers.answer: Each manager secretly chooses a sea zone/home port and a London cash bid (a firm needs at least one ship); a closed home port is allowed. Hobnob is an alternative with no bid, trade, or dividends, but still expenses and retains its prior dividend marker. Bids are revealed simultaneously, while strategy cards stay facedown until the relevant Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency’s operations, matching firms reveal strategy, roll one die per £1 bid and pay the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful bid dice (1s/2s), potentially negative; a successfully trading President’s initiative is calculated the same way from its ships. After the President’s Trade success, fill in ascending initiative order, with the President choosing ties. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governors have acted and the Chairman chooses tied initiative. Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and may fill up to ships + 1 open orders, tracing a route starting at home port through its own filled route; it can fill an order only once itself. Firm revenue goes to its India treasury. It may refill an order another trader or the Company filled that turn, and the Company may refill firm-filled orders. An order filled earlier pays half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies section gives bid timing/checks and initiative; order-fill timing, tie-breaks, capacity/routes, repeated order and half revenue, and value increments.

answers.answer: At Revenue, firms pay expenses before the Company, in initiative order (then other firms; ties by manager’s most windows and PM clockwise order). Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of firm share count or firm Value, paid from London and/or India treasuries. After expenses, dividends may be paid only from India: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager, though with manager consent a shareholder can forgo payments on any number of shares. Record total actual cash paid out as the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India cash to London. If a firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued: shareholders go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, charter to family side, while workshops stay invested. Rescue can use emergency investments under normal share/workshop rules (even if the ten-share limit blocks new shares), pay expenses, discard remaining cash, and lower Value one per emergency investment; alternatively merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and cover the failing firm’s shortfall.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, dividend funding/calculation and marker rules stated. Insolvency section gives dissolution destinations and rescue by emergency investment or one other firm.
